rules.name: Core coursework (PhD students, or MSTP students)

children.name: Core Courses (with nine quarters of NEPR 280)
Advanced Courses: six pre-approved units, one course of 3 units or more
One of NEPR 201, NEPR 203, NEPR 207 or NEPR 208
Two of those quarters for 2 units
Advanced Courses: one pre-approved course of 3 units

rules.desc:
Required courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a 3.0 (B) or better. MSTP students will take NEPR 209, NEPR 211, NEPR 212, and NEPR 288. MSTP students will take one of NEPR 201, NEPR 203, NEPR 207, or NEPR 208. MSTP students will also take either NEPR 202 or NEPR 204.
Students must also complete the Stanford Immersive Neurosciences (SIN) Boot Camp.
Students must complete special sessions in neuroanatomy. (Not required for MSTP students.)
9 quarters of NEPR 280 (Journal Club) are required. MSTP students in the Neurosciences PhD program are required to take 3 quarters of Journal Club and at least 2 quarters must be taken for 2 units.

rules.name: Statistics and Reproducible Research
rules.desc: Students must complete BIOS 217 as well as one graduate statistics course from the list below; pre-approval is required.
rules.notes: Required courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a 3.0 (B) or better.

children.name: Foundations of Statistics and Reproducible Research

rules.name: Graduate Research
rules.notes: Students must complete a graduate research course (NEPR 399) every quarter with a 3.0 (B) or better upon joining a thesis lab until satisfying the 135 minimum units required.

rules.name: First Author Publication
rules.desc: Students must publish at least one first-author paper in a peer-reviewed major scientific journal on the defended work before completing the PhD degree.

rules.name: Qualifying exam
rules.desc:
Passing a comprehensive qualifying examination given by the student’s advisory committee is required for admission to PhD candidacy.
The qualifying exam assesses whether the student is ready to advance to candidacy by proposing a thesis project of acceptable scope and feasibility, that the student is prepared to take on the research, has justified the research in terms of background, significance and innovation and has a well-justified approach.
The qualifying exam includes a qualifying exam proposal in the style of an NIH NRSA proposal and a written rigor document which outlines how the proposed research has addressed NIH's four key areas of rigor as well as a plan for dissemination for research outcomes and products.
The qualifying exam must be taken by May 31 of the second year for students starting AY26-27, and by June 30 for those starting AY25-26 and earlier.

rules.name: Oral Examination
rules.desc: Students must defend the dissertation in a University Oral Examination that includes a public seminar.

rules.name: Dissertation
rules.desc: Students are required to prepare a PhD dissertation that is the result of an independent investigation accomplished while enrolled in the program that contributes to knowledge in an area of neuroscience.

transferPolicy: Refer to University policy on Transfer Work
reviewNotes: The audit checks 135 units, BIOS 217 and one graduate statistics course of 3 or more units, and NEPR 399, each required course letter graded at B or better. PhD students take the NEPR core courses with nine quarters of NEPR 280 and three quarters of NEPR 299 rotations; MSTP students instead take NEPR 209, 211, 212 and 288, one of NEPR 201, 203, 207 or 208, NEPR 202 or 204, and three quarters of NEPR 280 (two of them for 2 units), with no rotations. Checked by hand: the pre-approved advanced courses (six units with one course of 3 or more, or one 3-unit course for MSTP students), the SIN Boot Camp, the neuroanatomy sessions (not for MSTP students), a first-author paper, the qualifying exam, the oral exam and the dissertation.
